reels.caption:
.

PRISMA OFFICE BUILDING

Architect: Amirali sharifi @the.nuance.studio
Visualisation: @aroc.visual.studio
Video : @hamed.aliasgari

PRISMA is an office building shaped by geometry, light, and context.
We tried to turn a simple site regulation-a 45-degree cut for the neighboring setback-into the main concept of the project. By repeating and extending this angle, we developed a sequence of vertical layers that define both the façade and the internal organization. Each layer filters daylight, provides privacy, and orients the working spaces toward softer light and better views.

Our intention was to design an office environment that feels dynamic yet calm, where the façade and interior work as one continuous system. The same material extends from the exterior to the inside, creating spatial coherence and allowing the architecture to breathe between openness and solidity. PRISMA transforms a geometric rule into a living rhythm of form, shadow, and reflection.

يروزهى PRISMA يك ساختمان ادارى است كه از منطق هندسه، نور و بستر خود شكل كرفته است. در اين طرح تلاش كرديم يك قانون سادهى سايت - پخ ۴۵ درجه اى براى رعايت حريم همسايه - را به ايدهى اصلى طراحى تبديل كنيم. اين زاويه با تكرار و امتداد خود، پوسته هايى عمودى را شكل داد كه هم ساختار نما را تعريف مى كنند وهم سازمان فضايى داخل را. هر پوسته نورى كنترل شده ايجاد مى كند, حريم را حفظ مى كند وفضاهاى كارى را به سمت نور غير مستقيم و ديد مطلوب تر هدايت مى كند.
هدف ما خلق محيطى ادارى بود كه در عين سادكى و نظم، پويايى درون خود داشته باشد؛ جايى كه نما وفضا امتداد يكديكر باشند. مصالح مشابه از بيرون تا درون ادامه يافته تا وحدت بصرى و فضايي شكل كيرد، و بنا ميان صلبيت و شفافيت, ميان نور و سايه تنفس كند. PRISMA تلاشى است براى تبديل يك قانون هندسى به بيانى زنده از
فرم وانور.

reels.caption:
Hidden Staircase Concept
Hidden staircase is very convenient — but it's more than just a functional solution.

I came up with this concept about six months ago and originally shared it on my YouTube channel. Today, I'm finally posting it here.

At some point, this video started appearing all over Instagram without me — back when I was only focused on YouTube. Still, I wanted to share it here myself, the way I see it.

I'm a 3D concept designer, and while the idea was inspired by something I once saw, this is my own interpretation — rethought and redesigned through my perspective.

This is not AI.
This is a fully handcrafted 3D work.

Looking at it now, I can already see what I would improve — and that's part of the process.

What do you think — should I develop this idea further?
